reasons.demand: PROVISIONAL, pending replies (0 of 20 emails sent as of 2026-10-24). Market signals only: paid permit-lead products exist and charge $15-$149/month (Permit Ledger $14.99, Construction Monitor ~$96/mo historic, PermitGrab $149), so trades do pay for permit lists; Detroit alone issues ~465 trades + ~100 building permits a week. No Detroit-specific buyer has said yes yet.
reasons.repeat_use: Weekly list is subscription-shaped by nature; permits renew every week and the sheet is only useful fresh.
reasons.competition: National players (Construction Monitor, BuildZoom, Dodge, ConstructConnect, PermitGrab, Permit Ledger, Apify permit scrapers) cover permits generically; none found that is Detroit-specific or trade-tagged for small shops. But the data is free and the moat is thin: anyone can rebuild it.
reasons.license: Detroit Open Data Portal policy (Exec. Order 2015-2) says data may be redistributed and re-used by business, and the datasets are public with no per-dataset license. BUT detroitmi.gov/Privacy, linked from the portal footer, says commercial use is prohibited without written permission. Scored 3 until Nick gets written confirmation from the ODP team (see needs_nick.md); would be 4-5 with it, 1 without.
reasons.build_effort: refresh.py already produces the weekly CSV/HTML/PDF from core in one run; remaining work is a mailing list, Stripe/Lemon Squeezy checkout and a Monday cron. Days, not weeks.
